title: Last Digit of a Large Power
description: Given two non-negative 64-bit integers `base` and `exp`, compute and return the last decimal digit (the ones digit) of `base^exp`. Follow the standard mathematical convention `0^0 = 1`.
hints: Only `base % 10` affects the last decimal digit of any power.
Compute `(base % 10)^exp % 10` using binary exponentiation in O(log exp) time, which naturally returns `1` when `exp == 0`.

examples.explanation: 7^4 = 2401 ends in 1, so 7^100 = (7^4)^25 also ends in 1.
By convention 0^0 = 1, so the last digit is 1.
